We just moved to Reno in April and have been slowly exploring in and around Reno. We went to or first Aces games last night and had a blast. I was wondering what spots are your favorites?

I like Oxbow park/nature preserve.It is a little less well known than the other parks but still on the river so you get great views and scenery without as many people around. Because its a nature preserve it feels more like a walk in the woods rather than a well manicured park, but the paths are still well maintained and clear. If you're looking for local restaurants and/or nightlife I would be happy to post a comprehensive list. I worked in a few popular local restaurants for years before changing career paths so I can give you a pretty good list. If you're looking for more vigorous outdoor activities I can give a basic list but don't really know things like specific hiking trails. Normally I would say go float the river but there's almost no water right now.

Hey thanks! Oxbow sounds nice! I'm starting to miss forests a little. And taking a walk through some woods sounds nice. We're into more urban activities over hiking, but we are planning to get some urban bikes for cruising. I'd love to see a list of restaurants! We def want check out the knitting factory, but haven't made it out yet. The river is still lovely even though it's low.

So I'll break the list down into categories, many will have crossover so the same names might be in several categories. Breakfast: All locals love Peg's. It's popular and the food is good but I honestly think PJ's on Wells Ave has better breakfast food and you can get a Bloody Mary there. Also good breakfast (and lunch) down that way is Cafe Deluxe. For weekend brunch hit up Old Granite St Eatery or Creme. All offer fairly standard breakfast brunch fair, Peg's or PJ's offer more classics (Eggs Benedict, French Toast, Etc.) Cafe Deluxe has many Vegetarian/vegan choices, Granite St., and Creme have more haute brunch fare

Lunch: Sup, Midtown Eats, Granite St., Campo, Greatful Gardens, Cafe Deluxe. Granite and Campo I feel are better for business lunches or a leisurely day. Midtown and Granite St. offer New American, higher end sandwiches,salads and table service. Sup (pronounced Soup) has all house-made soups,salads and sandwiches,order at the counter but a server brings out your food. Campo is high end yet simple Italian, has more American offerings at lunch (sandwich, burgers,etc) Deluxe and Grateful offer lighter and more veg/vegan options.

Casual to mid-level dinner: Campo, Granite St., Midtown Eats, The Gas Lamp, Pignic Pub and Patio, Bangkok Cuisine, Thai Chili, Reef Sushi, Sushi Lover, Noble Pie and JJ's Pie. Yes a lot of repeats here so just think the above descriptions but dinner, full courses, etc. The Gas Lamp would be on par with the aforementioned but only do dinner. Pignic is fun, you grill your own stuff, bring it or buy it there. Bangkok and Thai are obvious but again locals all say Bangkok but I like Thai Chili better. Reef Sushi/Sushi Lover, obvious but there are a lot of choices there and I don't want to kick off the great Reno Sushi debate of 2015, suffice to say they're both really good. Noble Pie/JJ's Pie, good local pizza.

Fine Dining: 4th St Bistro, Beaujolais Bistro, LuLou's, La Famiglia. All are fine dining, formal atmospheres. 4th St and LuLou's have the most haute cuisine in town. Personally, and most would agree 4th St is the best. Beaujolais is formal French fare, La Famiglia formal Italian. Phew, well that's it. I'm sure I missed a few things but that covers some pretty big bases. Fellow locals feel free to chime in.
